SPINE DESTINATIONS CANNOT BE RESOLVED AGAINST THE DECLARED PARENT CHAIN, and this is new. (a) The relation is not spelled `parent`/`parent_table`/`parent_view`/`parent_name` -- all four return ZERO edges. It is tables[].columns[].child_view, an edge from parent to child. A reader on any `parent*` spelling finds 0 edges and concludes every view is a root; I did exactly that on the first pass and the run reported 299 lowest-common-ancestor crosses that do not exist. (b) The relation covers 89 of 126 tables, leaving 37 roots of which 24 are _PIVOT_VW views. (c) Consequently only 145 of 5199 full-name destinations (2.8%) are reachable by walking the chain. A verifier following BUILD_RULES 4 literally would classify 5054 arrows as LCA crosses and instantiate a cross layer this LOB does not need. STAGE 1 MUST resolve spine destinations by view-name containment, not by child_view, and must not read a child_view miss as a cross.

A SECOND DESTINATION NAMING FORM, not previously recorded. Of 5496 spine arrows, 5199 name the FULL view name and 297 name an UNQUALIFIED SEGMENT -- 8 distinct: PARTY_PROPERTY (145), MEMBER_DETAILS (78), PROPOSER_DETAILS (67), RISK_LIST (2), QUOTE_PARAM_DETAILS (2), RISK_COVER (1), INSURED_DETAILS (1), POLICY_DETAILS (1). None is a table_name in the index, so a resolver that looks destinations up returns None on 297 arrows. All 297 are segments of their own origin view name, so a segment fallback is total on this map.

The build's child_key_components reader binds ONE spelling per role (name / value / expression / leg_backing) from the profile, and accepts none of the alternates CONVENTIONS.json declares mandatory (leg / component / maps_to for names; raw / column / source_column for values). Harmless on THIS map -- only name, value, leg_backing, expression, resolved_on_view, note and one `column` occur -- but a live hazard for the next re-issue, which is exactly what the declaration exists to prevent. Widen the reader, or state in the profile that it deliberately does not.
